messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for tenant 'acme-corp' on dedicated-cluster 'dedicated-eu-42'. Alert keys: reserved_capacity_throttling_high, request_error_rate_spike. Current: 5m error rate 4.9% (baseline 0.2%), p95 latency 2600ms (baseline ~180ms). Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-12345

PagerDuty: Paging Sam (oncall) -> Trigger: PD-12345. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> eng-sre -> eng-runtime.

Sam (oncall): Ack. I'm taking this. TL;DR: tenant latency + errors on dedicated-eu-42. Impact visible to acme-corp.

Sam (oncall): Quick checks: gating dashboard shows throughput steady but batcher queue depth for tenant spikes. KV cache evictions up 10x. I'm dropping into cluster.

Maya (eng-runtime): @Sam seeing same. batcher backlog growth around 14:10 UTC. adapter CPU ~95% on set of pods serving acme-corp. KV cache miss ratio ~0.76 (norm ~0.05). Possibly cache thrash after rollout last night?

Sam (oncall): Can you grep logs for OOMs or cache eviction reasons?

Maya (eng-runtime): Running fetch now. Cmd: ```kubectl -n rw logs deploy/dedicated-eu-42-batcher --since=10m | grep "evict" -i | tail -n 50```

Maya (eng-runtime): Logs show repeated: `kvcache: shard eviction due to memory pressure` and this trace: ```2026-03-14T14:09:13Z runtime/cache.go:244 evict shard=7 used=1.9GB limit=1.6GB```

Juan (eng-sre): Paging metrics also show node-level memory ballooning on hosts backing that pool. Could be noisy tenant using lots of KV. Any config changes to tenant limits?

Sam (oncall): Not that I'm aware of. Customer hasn't requested more capacity. Looks like reserved pool sizing insufficient for current workload + recent prefix cache increase.

Kyle (infra): I can spin short-lived burst instances into the dedicated pool, but that takes ~3-4 minutes to warm. Suggest enable burst capacity and route new requests to fallback small-latency model until burst is provisioned.

Maya (eng-runtime): Agree. Fallback variant available: `redwood/small-latency-v2` (lower mem KV). Routing can be changed via policy: ```POST /v1/routing/policy -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","policy":"route_to_fallback","ttl_s":900}'```

Sam (oncall): Doing that now. Applying routing override to send 100% new traffic to fallback for 10m.

Sam (oncall): Command run: ```curl -X POST https://console.api/routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","route":"fallback","duration":600}'```

Sam (oncall): Route applied. Observing immediate drop in p95?

Maya (eng-runtime): p95 dropped to ~320ms for routed requests within 45s. Overall cluster p95 now at 720ms (was 2.6s). Error rate slowly declining. Good sign.

PagerDuty: PD-12345 acknowledged by Sam (oncall).

Juan (eng-sre): I'll provision two burst nodes into the reserved pool now (type: c6i-gpu-small). Kube autoscaler will attach, but need infra approval for short-term capacity.

Kyle (infra): Approved. Spawning nodes. ETA ~3:30.

Maya (eng-runtime): While nodes come up, I'll patch batcher to reduce per-tenant KV memory cap from 1.6GB -> 1.2GB to avoid thrash. Will roll with 2 replicas to avoid restart storm.

Maya (eng-runtime): Patch applied to deployment `dedicated-eu-42-batcher`, rolling update started. Patch diff: ```- kv_max_per_tenant_bytes=1717986918
+ kv_max_per_tenant_bytes=1288490188```

Sam (oncall): Noted. Observing decreased eviction events after first replica restarts.

Nina (customer-success): Heads up: acme-corp support inbox getting 5-6 reports of slow responses for their product search. Should we send an interim note?

Sam (oncall): Yes, please. Nina can you send a brief status update: "We've mitigated most latency by routing traffic to a lower-latency model and are provisioning burst capacity. Minimal data exposure. Engineers are working on a durable cap/scale fix." Keep it high level.

Nina (customer-success): On it. Drafted: "We've applied a temporary routing change to reduce latency and are provisioning additional capacity. We're monitoring and will update in 15 minutes." Sending now.

PagerDuty: PD-12345 escalated to eng-sre due to 12m without full resolution.

Juan (eng-sre): Burst nodes are up and joined the pool at 14:15 UTC. I tagged them `burst-acme-2026-03-14`. Reserved pool utilization dropped from 98% -> 62% after attach.

Maya (eng-runtime): After nodes join, KV eviction events stopped. Error rate now 0.4% (target <0.5%). I'll start rolling batcher replicas to stable config and remove the emergency cap tomorrow in a controlled rollout.

Sam (oncall): Good. I'll remove the temporary routing override in 10 minutes and observe.

Sam (oncall): Routing override removed at 14:20 UTC. Metrics: overall p95 stabilizing ~220-300ms. Error rate ~0.3%.

PagerDuty: PD-12345 resolved automatically by monitoring at 14:22 UTC (conditions cleared).

Sam (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Impact: acme-corp experienced elevated latency and a short error spike from 14:08-14:20 UTC while reserved pool saturated. Root cause (working hypothesis): recent increase in KV footprint combined with reserved pool right-sizing mismatch caused cache thrash + memory pressure on batcher pods.

Maya (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) Revert emergency routing and monitor (done). 2) Patch batcher default kv cap -> reduce or make adaptive (deployed emergency patch; schedule proper rollout). 3) Update autoscale policy for dedicated-eu-42 to add headroom and shorter spin-up for burst nodes. 4) Add tenant-level alert for kv cache miss ratio >0.5.

Juan (eng-sre): I'll create infra change to reduce node warm time and keep one spare warm node for reserved pools with heavy tenants.

Nina (customer-success): Customer notified and appreciative of quick update. They asked for a postmortem and assurance this won't recur. I'll coordinate comms with the account owner once PMs have the RCA.

Sam (oncall): Handoff: I'll own initial incident timeline & notes, Maya to author technical RCA, Juan to own infra/autoscale changes, Nina to handle customer comms. I'll be oncall for another hour then hand to next shift and drop summary.

Sam (oncall): Summary for handoff -> Impact window 14:08-14:22 UTC, acme-corp degraded, temporary routing + burst capacity mitigated. Current state: stable.

Kyle (infra): Noted. I'll follow up on node warm optimizations in infra backlog ticket INFRA-789.

Maya (eng-runtime): I'll open RCA PR with logs and graphs, target finish EOD.

Juan (eng-sre): I'll schedule a follow-up with eng-runtime to test adaptive KV cap algorithm in staging.

Sam (oncall): Thanks team. Closing thread for now. :thumbsup:

Sam (oncall): PagerDuty incident PD-12345 closed.

(automated) incident-bot: Please remember to file a postmortem for PD-12345 within 72h.
